ui_refresh_flow: Panel_EPD::display() has no explicit area; it applies the accumulated _range_mod
fillScreen marks the whole screen in _range_mod, so every current UI draw is a full-screen refresh

partial_refresh_support.api: Panel_EPD::display(x, y, w, h) and Panel_EPD::_update_transferred_rect
partial_refresh_support.alignment_limit: x is aligned down to an even pixel; width is expanded to include the pair
partial_refresh_support.empirical: A 476x240 probe region is consistently faster than a 540x960 probe region, so a real panel-area update is occurring.

probe_scenario.pattern: white background, 24px text, moving black block; measurements cover display()+waitDisplay() only

conclusions: The current obvious full-screen flash is caused by begin()/fillScreen, not by a missing driver partial-refresh capability.
Partial rectangular refresh is real and measurably faster, but quality-mode fixed cost is still high (about 1.5s for the probe region).
epd_text is the candidate default for full-page text UI because it keeps 4bpp/16-level output and is somewhat faster than quality.
epd_fast and epd_fastest are much faster, but are 1-bit and need dedicated ghosting/clarity validation before becoming the default.
For menu cursor movement, the next step is a small-region update with fast/fastest plus a periodic quality cleanup, not another full-screen redraw.
visual_review: pending operator observation; timing is measured, but perceived flash, text clarity, and ghosting require the physical screen.
next: P1: remove the unconditional full-screen fill from redraw paths, then update menu selection rows and article-list selection rows as partial regions.
